decision: Two visible continuity defects remain: the side-to-front head jump is now at 292.5-to-315, and the regenerated second look row is visibly slimmer than the first row, producing a width/proportion pop at the row boundaries.
method: Inspected the refreshed native direction and boundary sheets, complete state contact sheet, motion stills, and exact encoded final cells in a native strip with head enlargements for confirmation. All adjacent looks were considered in order. Acceptance was judged visually at the native 192 by 208 cell size; uniform mathematical yaw spacing was not required and numeric continuity metrics were not used as a gate.

blockers.evidence: 292.5 is still a strong sideward left-up head: the nose and chin sit well left and the side temple/rosette and ear dominate the silhouette. 315 presents a nearly frontal two-eye face with a centered chin. This reads as one conspicuously large head pivot at native size rather than a moderate neighboring head pose. The new 315 is different from the rejected source, but is too frontal to bridge the visible side view to the frontal-up end.
blockers.smallest_source_repair: Revise the 315 source head/upper neck into a visible intermediate left-up three-quarter view between the actual 292.5 and 337.5 cells. Keep both eyes visible, but make the far eye narrower and retain a clear leftward nose/cheek turn. Preserve the anatomical-left rosette attachment and the body registration.

blockers.evidence: The new row keeps approximately the same height and foot baseline, but the figure is visibly narrower through the face, chest/arms, wing spread, robe, and tail. At 337.5-to-000 these features expand together into the broader first-row figure. The head orientation at that seam is now credible, but the simultaneous whole-figure width change is visible at native size and cannot be explained by the small head tilt alone.
blockers.smallest_source_repair: Match the complete second source look row to the accepted first-row body and head footprint, using the actual 000/neutral figure as the proportion reference. Preserve the registered height and feet; correct the source figure width and component scale before re-encoding rather than stretching or patching the final encoded PNG.

same_character_and_rendering.evidence: The white/lavender hair, horns, violet eyes, pale robe, wings, curled scaled tail, and rosette remain recognizable as the same character. No separate art-style change is conspicuous.

head_body_proportions_and_practical_scal.evidence: The regenerated second look row is consistently slimmer at a similar height, causing the lateral proportion discontinuity documented above.

wings_tail_robe_attachment.evidence: Components stay attached and retain coherent design within the new row; their cross-row scale change is covered by the proportion blocker.

body_and_feet_registration.evidence: Standing feet and torso remain centered and at a consistent baseline. Running and jumping changes read as intended actions.

rosette_anatomical_left.evidence: The rosette remains physically attached on anatomical left, including the new final heads.

clipping_or_holes.evidence: No conspicuous clipped horn, wing, tail, robe hem, or foot, and no accidental transparent hole was found.

cardinal_semantics.evidence: 000 up, 090 right, 180 down, and 270 left remain recognizable. The final quadrant heads point upward, although the large yaw change into 315 remains a visual transition defect.

337_5_to_000_head_orientation.evidence: Both heads are near frontal and upward; there is no remaining profile-to-front head snap at this exact seam.

157_5_to_180_head_orientation.evidence: The bowed head transition reads naturally. The narrowing of the figure on entering the new row is covered by the lateral-scale blocker.

other_adjacent_head_transitions.evidence: Uneven pose spacing elsewhere does not by itself create another conspicuous identity or head-turn break.
